On May 28, 2019, 64 users were unbanned from Voat. These users are the same users above, save for those who were banned for Spam.

Obviously there are several recognizable usernames on this list, which is why these bannings were the subject of such controversy and drama. When bots and alts get banned, people tend not to blink an eye, but when legitimate users are banned, this encourages a deeper reflection on the justice of the bans. A central theme in the uproar caused by many of the bans captured in this report was the sense that the definitions of "Vote Manipulation" and "Doxxing" were not clear enough to warrant bans. Does vote manipulation require the use of alts, or is brgiading enough? What constitutes brigading if so? Must votes be applied en masse from a comment / submission history, or can consistently upvoting / downvoting a user's content when coming across them "in the wild" still be manipulation, if the encounters are frequent enough? Is doxxing still doxxing if the doxxed user played some role in connecting their own identity to their account? Perhaps the answers are obvious, but unless they are made clear to the users who are subject to these rules, bans are considered by many to be unjust.

Thus the One True Putt, meeting the expectations of those with the memories and attention spans necessary to see the history of Voat's administration in more than a fleeting light, apologized for seemingly hasty actions and reversed the bans, stating "I will not be processing further vote manipulation bans until we talk about the process as a community."

What may be deserving of mention in this report is the fact that only users from the latest wave of vote manipulation bans were unbanned, and that those from earlier waves remain banned (Screencap since in the future that banlog link will indicate different users as more users are banned). It may be that all of those banned in the earlier waves were truly guilty of the most blatant of vote manipulation -- but the same could be, and likely is true of some of those who were recently unbanned. Loath am I to complain when such good as these unbannings has already been done, but if the same standards are to apply to all, it might be worth (at least temporarily) unbanning some of those banned in previous waves until proper standards of vote manipulation can be worked out. But then we must ask, how far back must we go? Must all vote manipulation bans be reversed, even those that applied only to obvious alts and bots? Are we to go back only so far as there have been "legitimate" users banned? But then we have the petty issue of "devil's advocates" stepping forward to claim that the bots deserve such equal opportunity as the rest. How far back (and how absurd) must this solution become?

Much has transpired in recent days, and many questions remain to be asked. What does concern me about the recent announcement is Putt's closing comment:

As I look at this mess I've created, I realize that I should just stick to writing software and leave what is working alone

Knowing that a Votes feature has long been in the works, is this Putt signalling his intention to "leave what is working alone" and to work in the meantime on completing the Votes feature so that goats can decide for themselves on issues such as these, issues that, in the attempt to solve them, caused such drama to begin with? As sought after as the Votes feature is, I do fear the attitude that it can replace completely our dear admin, on whose authority as a moral agent this platform, in my opinion, depends. For democratic activity is only valuable in a society that is moral, and societies that distance themselves from the Most High are prone to becoming immoral.

But that is a discussion for another day. As always, stay vigilant, goats.
